title: Practice quiz: fractions and the water cycle
context: A made-up study set for the tests: four multiple-choice questions and two written ones.

questions.title: Half of a pizza
questions.question: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. How many slices make half of the pizza?

options.label: 4 slices
options.why: Half of 8 is 8 divided by 2, which is 4.

options.label: 2 slices
options.why: 2 slices is a quarter: 2 out of 8. This mixes up half with a quarter.

options.label: 6 slices
options.why: 6 out of 8 is three quarters, more than half.

options.label: 8 slices
options.why: 8 slices is the whole pizza, not half of it.

questions.title: The bigger fraction
questions.question: Which fraction is the biggest?
questions.hint: Think about how big each piece is, not how big the number is.

options.why: Splitting into fewer pieces makes each piece bigger, so 1/3 beats 1/4 and 1/8.
1/4 is smaller than 1/3: four pieces are smaller than three.
8 is the biggest number here, but eighths are the smallest pieces.

options.label: They are all the same
options.why: They all have a 1 on top, but the bottom number changes the size of the piece.

media.alt: Three bars: the 1/3 piece is longest, then 1/4, then 1/8.

questions.title: Puddles in the sun
questions.question: On a sunny day a puddle slowly disappears. Where does the water go?

options.label: Into the air as water vapor
options.why: The sun's heat turns the liquid water into a gas, water vapor. That is evaporation.

options.label: All of it soaks into the ground
options.why: Some can soak in, but a puddle on a hard path also disappears, so that is not the whole answer.

options.label: It stops existing
options.why: Water does not vanish; it changes form. The amount of water stays the same.

options.label: It turns straight into a cloud
options.why: Clouds form later, when the vapor cools high up and condenses. The puddle first becomes vapor.

questions.title: The cold glass
questions.question: Drops of water appear on the outside of a glass of ice water. What causes them?

options.label: Water vapor in the air cools and condenses
options.why: Warm air touches the cold glass, cools, and its water vapor turns back into liquid drops.

options.label: Water leaks through the glass
options.why: Glass does not let water through; the drops also appear on a sealed can.

options.label: The ice melts through the side
options.why: The ice stays inside. The drops come from the air outside.

options.label: Rain fell on the glass
options.why: This happens indoors too, where no rain falls.

questions.title: Explain the cycle
questions.question: In two or three sentences, how does water from the sea end up as rain over land?
rubric: 1 point: the sun evaporates sea water into vapor
1 point: the vapor cools, condenses into clouds and falls as rain
questions.model_answer: The sun heats sea water and it evaporates into water vapor. The vapor rises, cools and condenses into clouds, and the wind carries them over land, where the water falls as rain.

questions.title: Bonus: share a cake
questions.question: Bonus: three friends share 2 cakes equally. How much cake does each friend get, and how do you know?
questions.model_answer: Each friend gets 2/3 of a cake: cut each cake into thirds, that makes 6 pieces, and 6 pieces shared by 3 is 2 pieces each.
